A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EDiT/A-EDiT research. Their complete main text, figures, tables, algorithms and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including the relocated appendix material.

before.justification: V1 reports original Llama training experiments, downstream benchmark evaluations, throughput measurements, elasticity tests and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix A.3.

after.justification: V2 retains the original training, benchmark, throughput, elasticity and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The model-sharding scheme, forward-pass synchronization, pseudo-gradient penalty and asynchronous variant are unchanged. Algorithms 1-2 retain the same steps; the small synchronization-description edits in Section 3.1 do not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb-Edu and the same private pre-training corpus, the same eight downstream benchmarks, and the same straggler, bandwidth-constrained and elastic-training scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain the same comparator membership, including Baseline, Post Local SGD, DiLoCo and CO2/CO2* in their respective comparisons. The in-house benchmark comparison still uses Baseline and DiLoCo as comparators to EDiT/A-EDiT.

E3.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix A.2 retain the model configurations, training budgets, optimizer settings, synchronization intervals and evaluation metrics. The speed measurements and simulated straggler, bandwidth and elasticity procedures are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The pseudo-gradient component ablations and worker-loss analysis in Figure 7, synchronization profiling in Figure 9, and learning-rate/worker-count analysis in Figure 10 are retained. No robustness or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Figures 4 and 8 retain the same practice of averaging the last ten values for reported endpoints. There are no changes to seed information, repeated-run reporting, uncertainty intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings in Tables 1, 2, 5 and 6 and Figures 4-10 are unchanged. For example, EDiT's Table 1 average scores remain 44.82 on FineWeb-Edu and 34.96 on the in-house dataset. Relocating Table 5 and Figure 8 introduces no new results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 1 and its assumptions, and the proof in Appendix A.4 remain unchanged. Both versions state the same O(log(T)/sqrt(T)) convergence rate; equation-layout differences do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient sharded Local SGD, training stability through pseudo-gradient penalties, and asynchronous handling of persistent stragglers. The abstract's wording refinements do not change these claims' scope.

C2.justification: The interpretations of convergence, acceleration, scalability and ablation results remain the same. The conclusion retains both limitations: stragglers can harm A-EDiT performance, and the elastic-training simulation requires stopping and restarting when resources change.

D1.justification: V1 promises code release after acceptance; v2 states that code is available and provides a specific Atorch code location in the abstract's footnote. Conversely, Appendix A.3.1 removes the promise to open-source trained models. Hardware, hyperparameters and other implementation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and substantive positioning relative to earlier Local SGD and asynchronous methods. The introduction is condensed without changing the central novelty arguments.

P1.justification: V2 lightly revises the abstract and opening introduction, refines several explanatory sentences, and adds explicit references to Section 3.2 and Figure 10. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds ICLR 2025 publication headers and makes limited layout adjustments. Figure 8 moves from page 17 to page 16, while Table 5 moves from page 16 to page 17; their content is preserved, with no substantive figure or table redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a concrete code location instead of a future release promise, modestly improving reproducibility documentation, and makes small clarity and cross-reference improvements. Removing the model-release commitment leaves those plans less explicit, but does not establish withdrawal of an available resource. The methods, empirical evidence and theory remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
